  • Guidelines for visiting a urologist

What is urology?

Urology is a medical department that treats diseases related to the urinary passageway (urinary tract), such as the kidneys, ureters, bladder, and urethra, as well as the male reproductive organs, such as the prostate and testicles. If there is an abnormality in the function of the kidneys, which produce urine, and the urethra, which excretes urine from the body, various urinary problems may occur, such as frequent urination, bloody urine, pain during urination, and difficulty in urinating.

While urinary symptoms often have a significant impact on daily life, many people hesitate to see a doctor because they feel that it may be due to their age or that it is difficult to consult a doctor. However, behind urinary problems there may be hidden diseases such as cystitis, urinary tract stones, and enlarged prostate. Also, be careful as blood in the urine can be a sign of diseases of the kidneys, bladder, prostate, etc.
At our hospital, we use a combination of urine and blood tests, ultrasound examinations, etc. to confirm the cause and provide treatment according to the symptoms and disease. Urinary problems such as frequent urination and urinary leakage can often be improved with appropriate treatment, so it is important to consult your doctor as soon as possible if you have any symptoms that concern you.

If these symptoms occur, see a urologist.

If you have any of the following symptoms, please consider consulting a urologist.

Symptoms related to urination

  • Close to the toilet (frequent urination)
  • I wake up several times during the night to go to the toilet.
  • Difficulty urinating or taking a long time to urinate
  • Urine stops midstream
  • Feeling like urine remains even after urinating (residual urine sensation)
  • Blood in the urine (hematuria)

pain or discomfort

  • pain when urinating
  • pain in the lower abdomen
  • lower back or back pain

Other symptoms

  • There is urine leakage
  • suddenly feel a strong urge to urinate
  • I have concerns about male function.

These symptoms may be related to cystitis, urinary tract stones, or prostate disease.
If your symptoms persist or if there are any noticeable changes, it is important to check with your healthcare provider.

Main diseases treated in urology

In the urology department, we treat a wide range of diseases, including diseases of the urinary tract, from the kidneys to the urethra, and diseases related to the male reproductive organs.

diseases of the prostate

benign prostatic hyperplasia

Benign prostatic hyperplasia is a disease in which the prostate gland enlarges with age, compressing the urethra and making it difficult to urinate. It is more common in middle-aged and older men.
The main symptoms include frequent urination, nocturia, difficulty in urinating, and a feeling of residual urine. Depending on the severity of the symptoms, treatment such as drug therapy or surgery is performed.

prostate cancer

Prostate cancer is one of the most common cancers in men. In the early stages, symptoms are unlikely to appear and may be detected through a PSA test (prostate-specific antigen test) performed during a health checkup. As the disease progresses, urinary symptoms and hematuria may occur.

prostatitis

There are acute and chronic.
Acute prostatitis is often accompanied by fever and painful urination, and requires antibiotic treatment.
Chronic prostatitis has a variety of symptoms, including dull pain or discomfort in various areas such as the penis, scrotum, groin, and lower abdomen, frequent urination, pain during urination, and blood in the semen, and is often treated as an indeterminate complaint. One cause is mechanical stimulation of the prostate gland, such as from sitting for long periods of time (desk work, commuting, riding a bicycle, etc.).
Treatment is mainly a combination of lifestyle changes and drug therapy, but the treatment period may last several months.

bladder disease

cystitis

Cystitis is a disease caused by bacterial infection of the bladder. It is especially common in women.

Main symptoms
  • pain when urinating
  • Frequent urination
  • Feeling of residual urine
  • cloudy urine

In many cases, improvement can be expected with treatment with antibiotics.

overactive bladder

Overactive bladder is a disease in which the bladder contracts excessively, causing a sudden strong urge to urinate.
It may also be accompanied by frequent urination or urine leakage. Symptoms can be expected to improve with lifestyle changes and drug therapy.

urinary stones

Urinary tract stones are a disease in which stones form in the urinary tract, such as the kidneys, ureter, or bladder. If a urinary stone becomes stuck in the ureter, it may cause sudden and severe lower back pain.

Main symptoms
  • Severe lower back pain or lower abdominal pain
  • hematuria
  • nausea or vomiting

Depending on the size and location of the stone, treatment to wait for the stone to be expelled naturally or specialized treatment will be considered.

Urinary trouble

Many people may experience symptoms related to urination.

as a representative

  • Frequent urination
  • nocturnal urination
  • Urinary incontinence (urine leakage)

Urinary incontinence includes stress urinary incontinence, which occurs when urine leaks when coughing or sneezing, and urge urinary incontinence, which occurs when a person suddenly has the urge to urinate. Treatment methods are selected depending on the cause and symptoms.

infectious disease

Bacterial infections can occur in the urinary tract.

pyelonephritis

Pyelonephritis is a bacterial infection of the kidneys. You may experience fever, lower back pain, and discomfort when urinating. Appropriate antibiotic treatment is required.

sexually transmitted diseases

Among sexually transmitted diseases, there are also diseases related to the urinary system, such as urethritis. If you experience pain when urinating or discharge from the urethra, it is important to seek examination and treatment at a medical institution.

About sexually transmitted diseases that are common in both men and women

chlamydial infection

Chlamydia infection is the most common sexually transmitted infection in men. If the urethra is infected, it is called chlamydial urethritis.
After an incubation period of 1 to 3 weeks after infection, a small amount of clear to slightly whitish discharge may be seen from the urethral opening. The pain when urinating is often mild, and it is difficult to notice because there are few subjective symptoms.
As the infection progresses, the epididymis becomes inflamed and epididymitis develops, which may be accompanied by swelling, pain, and fever in the scrotum. The throat can also be infected through oral sex, and in this case there are almost no symptoms, so you need to be careful.
Diagnosis is made by nucleic acid amplification technique (NAAT) using first urine. For throat infections, tests are performed using throat swabs or gargles.
Treatment is with oral antibiotics. You should refrain from sexual activity for 7 days after starting treatment. In addition, a retest will be conducted two weeks after the start of treatment to confirm that the test has turned negative. To prevent reinfection (so-called ping-pong infection), it is important that your partner also undergoes testing and treatment at the same time.

gonorrhea infection

Gonorrhea is the second most common sexually transmitted infection after chlamydia. When the urethra becomes infected, it becomes gonococcal urethritis.
The incubation period is relatively short, from 2 to 7 days, and it is characterized by severe pain when urinating and a large amount of yellow to green purulent discharge.
Diagnosis is made by microscopic examination of urethral secretions and first urine, and by nucleic acid amplification. Additionally, as mixed infection with chlamydia is observed in approximately 30% of gonorrhea infections, it is recommended that both tests be performed at the same time.
Treatment is primarily with antibiotic injections. This is because oral medications may not be sufficiently effective due to the increase in resistant bacteria. As with chlamydia, it is important to refrain from sexual activity for 7 days after treatment and to treat your partner at the same time.

Mycoplasma/ureaplasma infection

Infections with Mycoplasma and Ureaplasma are also relatively common sexually transmitted infections.
After an incubation period of 1 to 5 weeks after infection, urethral discharge and discomfort/pain when urinating may be seen. In addition, a throat infection may cause a mild sore throat or discomfort, but it is often asymptomatic.
Diagnosis is made by PCR testing using urine or throat samples.
Treatment is with oral antibiotics, which are typically administered in a single dose or for several days to a week. However, in recent years, the increase in drug-resistant bacteria has become a problem, and retesting may be recommended after treatment.

genital herpes

An infection caused by the herpes simplex virus (HSV-1 or HSV-2) that causes blisters and ulcers to form on the genitals.
In the first infection, small blisters appear 2 to 10 days after infection, which rupture to form painful ulcers. It may also be accompanied by systemic symptoms such as fever, fatigue, and swollen lymph nodes.
Once infected, the virus stays latent in the nerves and can repeatedly recur when triggered by fatigue or stress. In fact, most cases of genital herpes are recurrent cases.
Diagnosis is often made based on characteristic skin and mucous membrane findings, and additional tests are performed as necessary. Treatment is basically oral antiviral drugs, and in severe cases, intravenous therapy is used. However, the virus itself cannot be completely eliminated and there is a possibility of recurrence.

warts acuminata

It is a disease in which wart-like lesions occur around the genitals and anus due to infection with the human papillomavirus (HPV).
The lesions are cauliflower-shaped or cock-comb-shaped and pink to brown in color. There are often no noticeable symptoms, but it may be accompanied by itching or discomfort.
Diagnosis can often be made by visual inspection, but tissue tests may be performed if necessary.
Treatments include topical medications, cryotherapy with liquid nitrogen, laser therapy, and surgical excision. However, the recurrence rate is high at 20-30%, and multiple treatments may be required.

candidiasis

This is an infection caused by Candida (fungus), which is relatively rare in men, but can present as balanitis.
Redness, eczema, blisters, and white deposits can be seen on the glans, accompanied by itching and discomfort. Risk factors include diabetes, phimosis, and steroid use.
Diagnosis is made by culture testing using specimens from the affected area.
The basic treatment is topical antifungal drugs.

syphilis

Syphilis is a sexually transmitted disease caused by Treponema pallidum, and as it progresses, various symptoms appear. After infection, the progression is as follows:

  • Stage 1: Lumps and ulcers at the infected site
  • Stage 2: Generalized rash and lymph node swelling
  • Incubation period: Asymptomatic
  • Stages 3-4: Disorders to the nervous system and cardiovascular system

It may be mistaken for a spontaneous recovery because the symptoms temporarily disappear, but if left untreated, it can lead to serious complications. Diagnosis is through blood tests, and treatment involves administering antibiotics (mainly penicillin) for a certain period of time. In recent years, the number of syphilis patients has been on the rise in Japan, and the disease is spreading not only among young people but also among middle-aged and elderly people.

Diseases specific to men

Men may consult a urologist for the following diseases and symptoms:

andropause

Andropause is a condition in which men get tired easily, lose motivation, and change their mood due to a decline in male hormones as they age. Treatment will be considered depending on symptoms and test results.

ED (erectile dysfunction)

ED refers to the inability to obtain or maintain a sufficient erection. The cause is related to various factors such as lifestyle, aging, and stress.

Women's urinary problems

Women may experience the following urinary problems:

  • cystitis
  • urinary incontinence
  • Frequent urination

Urinary leakage may occur due to weakening of the pelvic floor muscles due to childbirth or aging. Improvement may be expected through lifestyle changes and treatment.

Main tests performed in urology

Urology departments perform various tests depending on symptoms and suspected diseases.

urine test

By examining the components of the urine, we check for infection and presence of blood in the urine.

blood test

This is done to check kidney function, inflammation status, prostate status, etc.

Ultrasound examination (echo)

This is a test that uses images to check the condition of the kidneys, bladder, prostate, etc. It is one of the tests that places less stress on the body.

PSA test

This is a blood test done to check for the possibility of prostate cancer.

image test

If necessary, a CT scan may be performed to investigate conditions such as urinary tract stones in detail.

Main treatments in urology

Urology provides a variety of treatments depending on the disease and symptoms.

drug therapy

Medications are used depending on the symptoms and cause of the disease.

example
  • Drugs for treating enlarged prostate
  • Medications for overactive bladder
  • Antibiotics

Review of lifestyle habits

Lifestyle adjustments may be made to improve urinary problems.

  • Review of water intake
  • Improving urinary habits
  • Adjustment of eating habits

Guidelines for visiting a urologist

If you have any of the following symptoms, it is important to consult a medical institution as soon as possible.

  • Blood in the urine (hematuria)
  • pain when urinating
  • Continuing to urinate frequently or leak urine
  • Difficulty urinating
  • I have severe pain in my lower back or back

Symptoms of urinary tract diseases can often be expected to improve if the cause is identified early and appropriate treatment is performed.
If you have trouble urinating or have any symptoms that bother you, it is important to consult a medical institution without forcing yourself to hold back.
